request.system:
You explain a fitted credit-risk model to a credit risk manager who is not a data scientist. You receive the facts about one model and write a short explanation of what drives its predictions of default.

# The text

- Write 5 to 8 sentences in plain English, most important drivers first.
- Mention an interaction when it matters for the model's predictions.
- Say only what the facts support. Do not round a weak effect up to a strong one, and do not add knowledge about credit risk that the facts do not show.
- When the facts do not settle something, say so ("the data do not settle whether ...") or leave it out.

# The answer

Return one JSON object with one list, `sentences`, each with an `id` (1, 2, 3, ...) and its `text`.
messages:
These are the facts about the model.

Model: a gradient-boosted tree model of depth 2 (XGB2), fitted to predict whether a credit applicant defaults (50,000 applicants). Effects are on the log-odds scale: positive values raise the risk of default. Every band is a 95% band from 100 refits of the model on resampled data.

Features, in the order of their share of the model's importance:
- `utilization`: revolving credit utilization: the share of the credit limit in use (0 to 1).
  Share of importance 26.8% (95% band 24.3% to 29.5%); rank 1 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.283: -0.65; 0.283 <= x < 0.46: -0.27; 0.46 <= x < 0.606: +0.1; 0.606 <= x < 0.653: +0.7; 0.653 <= x < 0.719: +1.32; 0.719 <= x < 0.801: +2; x >= 0.801: +3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +3.07, 95% band [+2.55, +3.19]).
- `n_delinquencies`: number of past delinquencies on the credit file (0 to 6).
  Share of importance 15.8% (95% band 14.2% to 17.7%); rank 2 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): 0: -0.4; 1: +0.2; >= 2: +0.5 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.88, 95% band [+0.76, +0.92]).
- `income`: annual income in US dollars.
  Share of importance 8.6% (95% band 7.6% to 9.8%); rank 3 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 36,200: +0.328; 36,200 <= x < 69,200: 0; x >= 69,200: -0.3 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.79, 95% band [-0.87, -0.57]).
- `history_months`: length of the credit history in months.
  Share of importance 7.6% (95% band 6.5% to 8.7%); rank 3 to 4 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 80.5: +0.3; 80.5 <= x < 212: -0.002; x >= 212: -0.18 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.66, 95% band [-0.75, -0.44]).
- `dti`: debt-to-income ratio (0 to 0.6).
  Share of importance 5.8% (95% band 4.4% to 6.4%); rank 5 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): x < 0.431: -0.08; x >= 0.431: +0.2 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.31, 95% band [+0.17, +0.39]).
- `n_inquiries`: number of recent credit inquiries.
  Share of importance 3.7% (95% band 2.1% to 4.2%); rank 6 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): <= 1: -0.07; >= 2: +0.1 (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.31, 95% band [+0.17, +0.37]).
- `num_dependents`: number of dependents (standardised).
  Share of importance 1.1% (95% band 0.1% to 2.1%); rank 7 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile -0.05, 95% band [-0.20, +0.07]).
- `age`: age of the applicant in years.
  Share of importance 0.8% (95% band 0.2% to 2.1%); rank 7 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.01, 95% band [-0.17, +0.12]).
- `months_at_address`: months at the current address (standardised).
  Share of importance 0.6% (95% band 0.1% to 2.1%); rank 7 to 9 among 9 features.
  Curve (logit contribution by value): no movement resolved at this sample size (net change from the 5th to the 95th percentile +0.09, 95% band [-0.03, +0.21]).

Interactions: the model has 31 pairs. The larger ones:
- `utilization & n_delinquencies`: share of importance 18.1% (95% band 15.6% to 18.8%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0994 to 0.752: +0.71 (95% band +0.59 to +0.98) when `n_delinquencies` = 0, +5.86 (95% band +4.66 to +5.89) when `n_delinquencies` = 2.
  Effect of `n_delinquencies` from 0 to 2: -0.42 (95% band -0.48 to +0.04) when `utilization` = 0.0994, +4.72 (95% band +3.75 to +4.68) when `utilization` = 0.752.
- `history_months & n_inquiries`: share of importance 3.4% (95% band 2.0% to 4.1%).
  Effect of `history_months` from 24.2 to 343: -0.23 (95% band -0.47 to -0.08) when `n_inquiries` = 0, -1.33 (95% band -1.68 to -0.86) when `n_inquiries` = 4.
  Effect of `n_inquiries` from 0 to 4: +0.99 (95% band +0.51 to +1.05) when `history_months` = 24.2, -0.12 (95% band -0.53 to +0.11) when `history_months` = 343.
- `utilization & income`: share of importance 1.0% (95% band 0.6% to 1.4%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0994 to 0.752: +2.87 (95% band +2.43 to +3.10) when `income` = 22,000, +3.22 (95% band +2.62 to +3.27) when `income` = 114,000.
  Effect of `income` from 22,000 to 114,000: -0.94 (95% band -0.98 to -0.45) when `utilization` = 0.0994, -0.60 (95% band -0.79 to -0.37) when `utilization` = 0.752.
- `utilization & history_months`: share of importance 0.9% (95% band 0.6% to 1.6%).
  Effect of `utilization` from 0.0994 to 0.752: +2.97 (95% band +2.37 to +3.11) when `history_months` = 24.2, +3.08 (95% band +2.61 to +3.20) when `history_months` = 343.
  Effect of `history_months` from 24.2 to 343: -0.72 (95% band -0.85 to -0.48) when `utilization` = 0.0994, -0.61 (95% band -0.78 to -0.30) when `utilization` = 0.752.
- 27 further pairs with a share below 0.5% each, together 5.8%.

Write the explanation.

content.text: {"sentences":[{"id":1,"text":"The model's predictions of default are driven mostly by revolving credit utilization, the share of the credit limit an applicant is using, which accounts for about 27% of the model's importance and is the single strongest driver."},{"id":2,"text":"Higher utilization raises the predicted risk of default, and the effect is steep at the high end: moving from the 5th to the 95th percentile adds about 3 units to the log-odds, with the effect strongest for applicants who have past delinquencies."},{"id":3,"text":"The number of past delinquencies is the second most important driver, at about 16% of importance, and having one or more raises predicted risk, with the largest increase between zero and one or two delinquencies."},{"id":4,"text":"Utilization and past delinquencies interact strongly, together about 18% of importance: utilization matters far more for applicants with two delinquencies (about +5.9 log-odds across its range) than for those with none (about +0.7), and the delinquency effect is likewise much larger at high utilization."},{"id":5,"text":"Income, length of credit history, and debt-to-income ratio each have smaller effects: lower income and shorter credit histories raise predicted risk, and a higher debt-to-income ratio adds a modest amount of risk."},{"id":6,"text":"Recent credit inquiries add a small increase in risk at two or more, and the effect of history length depends on the number of inquiries, though these interactions are minor compared with the main effects."},{"id":7,"text":"Age, number of dependents, and months at the current address show no effect that can be distinguished from zero at this sample size, so the data do not settle whether they matter for predicted default."}]}
